_review.scope: Only BRIEF-12.md Part C: conifer_forest-0..7 and @winter, jungle-0..7, deadforest-0..7 and @winter, bamboo-0..7 and @winter. Existing floor bases and all comparison art are outside the verdict scope.
_review.calibration: Good enough to ship beside the approved art. Species-appropriate narrow crowns, low umbrella pines, open larches and short broken stumps are acceptable. Failures are native-scale subject/cluster readability defects, not demands for extra detail or perfect botanical rendering.
_review.prior_review: art-drop/review/critic-r12C-0.json does not exist; no inherited passes apply.

checks.brief_and_named_reference: Read BRIEF-12.md, including its shared top-left lighting, dark outline, three-quarter overhead view, native density and placement requirements. Compared all eight treeline_forest output sprites and the autumn counterparts at native size and 4x. Also read original BRIEF.md and BRIEF-2.md for established style calibration.
checks.approved_art: Viewed all 24 approved output markers from six settings, summer/winter city, industry, slums, suburb and farmland examples, all 32 seasonal paddies, and grass/plains bases with all eight detail variants in all four seasons. Full 96x96 detail canvases retained in corrected comparison boards and individual grass/plains crops. Comparison assets receive no new verdict.
checks.forest_composites: All seven eight-sprite sets composited on appropriate existing ground in deterministic staggered forest placements, thinning into open ground. Inspected each forest at native 1x and exact nearest-neighbour 4x. Also inspected every set as aligned rows at 1x/4x. Crowns overlap naturally without a rectangular backing or per-cell grid; the two dense bamboo layouts fail subject clarity.
checks.every_file_8x: All 56 files visually inspected in fourteen four-sprite sheets at exact 8x, with a complete 48x48 sprite in each 384x384 panel. Sheets use the appropriate ground; independent full light/dark alpha proofs were inspected at 4x. No verdict was based only on thumbnail views.
checks.base_3x3: Not applicable: Part C contains no base textures. conifer_forest/deadforest floor-base files are pre-existing comparison ground, not Part C deliveries.
checks.peak_lattice_or_range: Not applicable: Part C contains no peaks. Forest lattice checks were performed for every tree set.
checks.one_cell_8x2_random_tiling: Not applicable to Part C: its 48x48 files are transparent individual trees, not edge-joining opaque terrain tiles. Randomized staggered forest placements exercise repetition and overlap. Approved opaque district/field tiles were laid out in comparison strips only, without an out-of-scope verdict.
checks.pixel_integrity: All 56 are 48x48 RGBA with exclusively 0/255 alpha and zero hidden RGB. All have transparent margins and opaque bottom-centre contact at (23,44). No blur, antialiasing, key-colour fringe, pale halo or clipped sprite edge found in the target art.
checks.lighting_palette_and_scale: Upper-left crown and wood highlights, lower/right shade planes, restrained greens, grey deadwood and blue-white snow fit the named treeline reference and approved art. No target is failed for palette, scale, light direction or registration.
checks.variation_and_winter: No exact duplicate files. Visual comparison finds sufficient silhouette differences among all eight members of each set; seasonal counterparts intentionally retain their layouts. All 24 winter sprites have visible snow on supported branches/leaves/wood ledges and remain populated. Bamboo 2 and 6 retain summer structural defects under winter paint.
checks.specific_problem_list: Identical crowns and noisy/muddy tree structure were checked directly. Egg-crate peaks, Swiss-cheese craters, classical ruins, stamped cyberpunk ground grids and flat orange autumn are not subjects in Part C; no expanded review or verdict on those files.

conifer_forest-0.notes: Broad irregular tiered spruce silhouette; upper-left foliage planes and dark lower branch edges read cleanly.

conifer_forest-1.notes: Slim fir has distinct stacked branch tiers and a readable central axis; narrowness is appropriate to its species.

conifer_forest-2.notes: Low umbrella-pine crown is deliberately broad; trunk and fork stay legible and distinguish it from the taller forms.

conifer_forest-3.notes: Full cedar-like triangular crown retains readable overlapping foliage planes and differs from 0 and 1.

conifer_forest-4.notes: Irregular broad pine has a clear trunk fork and asymmetric crown; does not repeat the umbrella-pine silhouette.

conifer_forest-5.notes: Open, sparse conifer shows connected branches and a central trunk; its gaps read as an intentionally open tree, not fringe debris.

conifer_forest-6.notes: Tall cypress-like column is a valid narrow species silhouette; restrained plane changes keep it solid and readable.

conifer_forest-7.notes: Wind-bent conifer has a strongly asymmetric top and layered lower branches; clearly different from the upright forms.

jungle-6.notes: Open fern-like radiating fronds and short trunk give a readable tree-fern silhouette.

jungle-7.notes: Asymmetric drooping fern-like fronds differ from 6; trunk and negative spaces stay readable.

deadforest-1.notes: Twisted S-shaped snag reads cleanly without tangles or isolated tips.

deadforest-2.notes: Open forked skeleton differs from the heavy snag; thin branches remain attached and legible.

deadforest-3.notes: Tall narrow broken trunk is a clear snag variant, with readable broken limbs and a small hollow.

deadforest-4.notes: Short hollow stump has a dark broken interior and legible flared roots; reduced height is intentional.

deadforest-5.notes: Leaning S-shaped tree has asymmetric ascending forks and a distinct root/trunk curve.

deadforest-6.notes: Second broken stump has a taller jagged break and different branch/root silhouette from 4.

deadforest-7.notes: Low twisted spreading dead tree is recognizably wood with connected limbs and a different silhouette.

bamboo-0.notes: Several long culms and open vertical channels remain visible; small leaf sprays support the bamboo reading.

bamboo-1.notes: Sparse asymmetric sprays leave the long segmented culms readable at native size; finer leaves remain subordinate.

bamboo-2.notes: At 1x the broad, almost closed crown and tightly converging lower culms read as a bush in a tapered bundle, rather than bamboo. At 4x/8x the upper foliage is a single dark mass with scattered light flecks; the stalks largely disappear into it. Open a few continuous background channels between the culms, expose their nodes farther up, and divide the canopy into narrow, directional leaf sprays instead of one triangular bush crown. See bamboo-row, bamboo-forest and bamboo-comparison proofs.

bamboo-3.notes: Leaning sparse clump keeps a readable main stem structure and open, directional side sprays.

bamboo-4.notes: Open channels separate the main culms; leaf clusters remain distinct enough to read as bamboo.

bamboo-5.notes: Few tall exposed segmented culms and sparse leaves give the clearest small bamboo silhouette.

bamboo-6.notes: The round, right-heavy crown is mottled with short alternating light/dark fragments, while the culms converge into one small foot. At 1x this becomes a noisy shrub silhouette; at 8x the many little fragments compete with the stems instead of defining bamboo leaf fans. Consolidate the flecks into fewer coherent drooping sprays, preserve clear gaps between several long culms and make their nodes readable. Keep the lean, but give the foliage a bamboo structure. See bamboo-forest and bamboo-comparison proofs.

bamboo-7.notes: Open spreading clump retains a readable fan of segmented culms and separated side sprays.

bamboo@winter-0.notes: Several long culms and open vertical channels remain visible; small leaf sprays support the bamboo reading. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-1.notes: Sparse asymmetric sprays leave the long segmented culms readable at native size; finer leaves remain subordinate. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-2.notes: Inherits the closed bush crown and bundled, converging culms of bamboo-2. The snow makes short horizontal stripes across the solid green crown, reinforcing a small snow-covered bush rather than separate bamboo sprays. Rework the culm separation and directional foliage with the summer counterpart, then put snow on the upper faces of those distinct sprays, retaining open channels. See bamboo@winter-row, bamboo@winter-forest and bamboo-comparison proofs.

bamboo@winter-3.notes: Leaning sparse clump keeps a readable main stem structure and open, directional side sprays. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-4.notes: Open channels separate the main culms; leaf clusters remain distinct enough to read as bamboo. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-5.notes: Few tall exposed segmented culms and sparse leaves give the clearest small bamboo silhouette. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-6.notes: Inherits bamboo-6's rounded shrub silhouette and fragmented foliage. The added white/blue dashes further chop up the canopy; at native size the snow, leaf flecks and stems make a busy mottled patch with weak bamboo structure. Simplify the underlying leaf fans and separate the long culms, then group the snow into a few supported caps on those sprays rather than scattering short dashes through the crown. See bamboo@winter-forest and bamboo-comparison proofs.

bamboo@winter-7.notes: Open spreading clump retains a readable fan of segmented culms and separated side sprays. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.
